clue.text: Sorry to see tree by the sea

parts.note: the ash is a common European tree
'by' can mean 'per', as in 'so much a head', giving A
the Med is the familiar short name for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to find a single tree spoiling the seaside view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' as A comes from its sense 'per' (ten pounds a head = ten pounds by the head); the Med is the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling regret or embarrassment over what one has done is to be sorry for it.

clue.text: Drudge to take exercise on

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercise lessons
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired labourer is ordered to do some exercise on top of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A peon is a lowly labourer doing menial work, which is what a drudge is.

clue.text: Sausage for French girl friend

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name, from Sally or Sarah
ami is French for friend, signalled by 'French'

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a sausage on behalf of a French girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs 'friend' across 'girl': AMI is the French word for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spiced, cured Italian sausage eaten in slices.

clue.text: First place Slavic language is of German duchy

indicators.note: 'First' asks for only the opening letter of the following word place

parts.note: Russian is the largest of the Slavic languages

explanation.surface: A claim about which Slavic tongue was spoken first in a German duchy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duchy of Prussia was a Baltic German state, so its adjective describes things belonging to that duchy.

clue.text: The maitre d'hotel awaited her order

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order means rearranging them, signalling an anagram of awaited her

explanation.surface: The restaurant's front-of-house man waited for her to place her order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' sounds like a diner's request, but it tells you to rearrange AWAITED HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A maitre d'hotel is the man in charge of the dining-room staff, a senior waiter.

clue.text: Cinema shows first French field mine

indicators.note: 'first' picks only the opening letter of the word French

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A cinema newsreel shows the first French minefield.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLEAPIT is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a grubby old picture house, supposedly infested with insects.

clue.text: As ages reflect I find a weapon

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word ages is turned round

parts.note: taken as written; turned it reads SEGA

explanation.surface: A thinker musing on the passing years stumbles on an ancient weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' looks like a verb of thinking, but it asks for the mirror image of 'ages', giving SEGA.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples.

clue.text: Concisely its a cheese insect

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A terse description of a bug found on a cheese board.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in few words or for a short time is doing it in brief, tersely.

clue.text: Train the Persians in rhetorical digression

indicators.note: to train is to shape or discipline, so the letters of the Persians are reshaped

explanation.surface: An instruction to drill Persian troops, buried in a speech's aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway or a verb of teaching, but it signals rearranging THE PERSIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A parenthesis is an aside inserted into a sentence, a brief digression from the main thread.

clue.text: She is navy meat or nothing when sweet

explanation.surface: A woman is described as naval rations, or nothing at all when sweetened.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny Adams was a girl murdered in 1867; sailors grimly named tinned meat after her, and 'sweet Fanny Adams' is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian murder victim, Royal Navy slang for tinned mutton, and in 'sweet FA' a byword for absolutely nothing.

clue.text: The wood trade

explanation.surface: A note about the timber business.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn pine or fir timber, and to deal is to do business or trade.

clue.text: Central idea, that a writer will paint in words

indicators.note: 'Central' asks for the middle letters of the word idea

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An author promises to set down the central idea in prose.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something verbally is to portray it, painting a picture with language.

clue.text: Remember what to do as visiting babysitter

definitions.text: what to do as visiting babysitter

explanation.surface: Advice on what a babysitter should do while minding someone's children.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a visiting babysitter must come to mind (look after) the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought that occurs to you is recalled; and a sitter has to arrive in order to look after the children.

clue.text: Not par for piratical dissention of language

indicators.note: 'Not' says the letters of the word par are left out of the mix
dissention is discord, so the remaining letters of piratical are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Pirates quarrelling over a word that isn't up to par.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P, A and R out of PIRATICAL and rearrange the leftover ITICAL, as 'Not' and 'dissention' direct.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic names the branch of Indo-European that includes Latin, so it describes a group of tongues.

clue.text: Persistently demanding various permutation

indicators.note: 'various' suggests a different arrangement of the letters of permutation

explanation.surface: A mathematician keeps insisting on trying every permutation.
explanation.definitionFit: An importunate person pesters others with pressing, repeated requests.

clue.text: Decoration or title book

parts.note: taken as written
a title is the name of a work
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Choosing between an ornament or a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is an object used to adorn or embellish.

clue.text: Left with gout seizing one

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so gout clasps one inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sufferer left with a painful attack of gout gripping one joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or a political wing; here it means departed, and 'seizing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has departed the house has left it.

clue.text: Tardy putting the old in bed

indicators.note: 'in' places the old word inside bed

parts.note: taken as written
late means former, as in 'the late president'

explanation.surface: Putting grandad to bed is a job done far too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' suggests elderly people being put to bed; here 'old' means former, as in 'the late king', and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that arrives behind time is late, overdue.

clue.text: Business trust ends on a thread

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: 'ends' asks for the first and last letters of the word trust

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's trust hangs by a thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is spun yarn used for sewing.

clue.text: Was beer shipped abroad by one?

parts.note: ex means former, what was once the case
porter is a dark, bitter beer

explanation.surface: A question whether a trader ever sent beer overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'something shipped abroad by one?': the one who sends goods overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that sells goods to foreign markets sends them out of the country.

clue.text: Previous or current father?

parts.note: past means previous, former
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a priest is a former one or the present one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, a spiritual father now serving it.

clue.text: Side point in a Scottish hat

indicators.note: 'in' says the point goes inside the hat

parts.note: a tam is a Scots woollen cap, short for tam-o'-shanter
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A team's emblem displayed on a Scottish bonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a group of players on one sports team.

clue.text: Conventional thought on sea current

parts.note: the main is a literary term for the open sea
a stream is a flowing current

explanation.surface: Received wisdom about ocean currents.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary, majority taste or opinion is what is conventional.

clue.text: Repetition learning rubbish of second degree

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: 'second' picks the second letter of the word degree

explanation.surface: Learning by repetition dismissed as nonsense, a second-rate qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes the second letter of 'degree', an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote is memorising through constant repetition.

clue.text: Controlling the next one across

explanation.surface: A note that the clue after this is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Running means in succession, as in 'three days running': each one coming next after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a business is managing it; things running are consecutive, one following the next.

clue.text: Kick the stage full of moonshine

parts.note: to boot is to kick
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Kicking over a stage set full of illicit liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg liquor is illegally made or smuggled spirits.
